free_tier.stated: 79,657 free eBooks, 'No fees, no registration, completely free'. The published collection metadata gives the real size: main collection 3,443,023 files / 1,064,736,252,276 bytes, generated collection (EPUB, MOBI, HTML) 2,681,516 files / 1,375,569,708,792 bytes, i.e. 6,124,539 files and 2,440,305,961,068 bytes (2.44 TB), metadata updated 2026-10-19.
free_tier.notes: The 79,657 counts titles; metadata.json counts files. Both were read on the same day and they describe different things, so neither is the other's check.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: one file per book per format. No per-file cap is published; the largest objects in the tree are audio ZIPs, and the file list is the only inventory.
per_object_cap.notes: A text file measured here was 772,386 bytes (Pride and Prejudice, plain text).

retention.stated: permanent: the mirroring guide describes a fixed collection that 'changes daily, as new items are added or updated', with no expiry clock.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered from the main site and from every mirror. The main site is not a bulk endpoint: 'This website is intended for human users only. Any perceived use of automated tools to access this website will result in a temporary or permanent block of your IP address.' Bulk is approved through rsync mirrors, which the mirroring guide documents.

interface_detail: plain HTTPS per file (https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/<id>/pg<id>.txt), an OPDS feed at /ebooks/search.opds/, a JSON OPDS2 feed 'currently available for testing', GUTINDEX.ALL and metadata.json for inventory, and rsync mirrors listed in MIRRORS.ALL.
tooling: wget/curl, rsync against any mirror, the OPDS feed for readers. The robot policy's own example is 'wget -w 2 -m -H "https://www.gutenberg.org/robot/harvest?filetypes[]=html"' - two seconds between requests, from the main site, for a bounded harvest.
chaining: The canonical public-domain text corpus to pair with LibriVox audio and Internet Archive scans of the same titles; a 2.44 TB rsync mirror can be filtered to the zip files only, which drops the audio weight.

limits.value: automated access from the main site is blocked by IP; 'Such blocks automatically expire after a few days'
the vendor's own harvest example uses wget -w 2 (two seconds between requests); mirrors are the approved bulk path

binding_note: At 1 TiB/month the main site blocks the caller long before any byte cap; the mirror network is the only path that carries that volume, and the mirror list is what makes the quota effectively unlimited.

identity_cost.detail: The home page states 'No fees, no registration, completely free'. No account exists to create.

reliability_note: Main-site IP blocks are automatic and last days; the generated collection is rebuilt in batches, so a mirror refresh sees traffic spikes rather than a steady delta.
confidence_note: The collection size is the vendor's own metadata.json, fetched here; one complete file was downloaded and hashed. What would raise it to measured for the bulk path is an rsync of a filtered subset from a mirror with a byte count, which was not run.

evidence.proved: 'Project Gutenberg is a library of 79,657 free eBooks' and '100% Free - No fees, no registration'
